name: VAWA Self-Petition (I-360)
summary: Self-petition for an abused spouse or child of a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, or abused parent of a U.S. citizen son or daughter.
confidentialityNote: Protected by 8 U.S.C. 1367. Restricted case: only assigned staff may open it. Never send notices to the abuser's address. Never put the abuser's name in reminders or messages.

forms.title: Petition for Amerasian, Widow(er), or Special Immigrant (VAWA)
Application to Adjust Status
forms.note: Concurrent filing only if the self-petitioner is an immediate relative (abuser is a U.S. citizen) or a visa is available.

forms.title: Application for Employment Authorization
forms.note: I-360 asks whether to issue a (c)(31) EAD on approval; a separate I-765 is only needed in other cases.

filing.where: See 'Where To File' on uscis.gov/i-360 (VAWA filings go to a dedicated address).

questions.label: Is it safe for us to call, text or mail you at the address and phone you gave?

options: U.S. citizen son or daughter (21 or older)

questions.label: Where and when did you live with the abuser?
If the marriage ended, or the abuser died or lost status, the date it happened
questions.help: You generally must file within 2 years of these events.

questions.label: Describe the abuse or extreme cruelty (physical harm, threats, control, isolation, threats about immigration)
How did you meet and why did you marry? (for spouses)
File Form I-485 at the same time?
Do you want USCIS to issue a (c)(31) work permit if approved?

checklist.label: Proof of the abuser's U.S. citizenship or permanent residence (copy of passport, birth certificate, naturalization certificate, Green Card, or anything showing their A-Number)
checklist.help: If you do not have it, tell us what you know. USCIS can sometimes check its own records.

checklist.label: Marriage certificate, divorce decree, or birth certificates proving your relationship to the abuser
Proof you lived together (lease, utility bills, school or medical records, mail to the same address)
Evidence of the abuse (police reports, protective orders, medical records, shelter letters, photos, counselor letters, affidavits)
Your personal declaration (staff will help you write it)
Your affidavit of good moral character
Police clearance or state background check from each place you lived 6 months or more in the last 3 years
Proof the marriage was real (joint insurance, lease, taxes, bank statements, photos, affidavits from people who know you)

coverLetter.re: Form I-360, VAWA Self-Petition - CONFIDENTIAL, protected under 8 U.S.C. 1367

points: The self-petitioner has a qualifying relationship with an abusive {{abuserStatus}}.
The self-petitioner resided with the abuser.
The self-petitioner was subjected to battery or extreme cruelty during the relationship.
The self-petitioner is a person of good moral character{{#goodFaith}} and entered the marriage in good faith{{/goodFaith}}.
